essentialPoints: Neutrons released by one fission event may be absorbed by other nuclei, causing further fission
This can cascade into a self-sustaining chain reaction

nodes.label: Dangers of large decelerations
nodes.objective: Explain the dangers caused by large decelerations, including brakes overheating and loss of control.
essentialPoints: Large decelerations can cause brakes to overheat
Large decelerations can cause loss of vehicle control

nodes.label: Estimating deceleration forces for road vehicles (HT)
nodes.objective: Estimate the forces involved in the deceleration of road vehicles in typical situations.
essentialPoints: Apply F = ma with estimated/typical vehicle mass and deceleration values to estimate braking forces

nodes.label: Ray diagrams for convex and concave lenses
nodes.objective: Construct ray diagrams to illustrate the similarities and differences in image formation between convex and concave lenses.
essentialPoints: Use standard lens symbols and construction rays (parallel-to-axis ray, ray through centre, ray through focus) to locate the image
Compare resulting image position/nature for convex vs concave lenses

nodes.label: Using/interpreting diagrams of radiation balance affecting Earth's temperature (HT only)
nodes.objective: Use information or interpret diagrams showing how radiation affects the temperature of the Earth's surface and atmosphere.
essentialPoints: Interpret given diagrams/data showing incoming solar radiation, reflected radiation and emitted infrared radiation
Relate the balance shown in such diagrams to changes in Earth's surface/atmosphere temperature

nodes.label: Step-up and step-down transformers
nodes.objective: Distinguish step-up and step-down transformers by their turns/pd ratios.
essentialPoints: In a step-up transformer, Vs > Vp (more turns on secondary than primary)
In a step-down transformer, Vs < Vp (fewer turns on secondary than primary)

nodes.label: Equation: transformer power (Vs Is = Vp Ip)
nodes.objective: Apply the equation for power input/output of an ideal (100% efficient) transformer.
essentialPoints: Vs × Is = Vp × Ip, assuming 100% efficiency
Vs×Is is power output (secondary), Vp×Ip is power input (primary)
Power measured in watts, W; given on the physics equation sheet

nodes.label: Identifying and handling anomalous results
nodes.objective: Recognise anomalous values, investigate their cause, and exclude them if due to poor measurement.
essentialPoints: An anomalous result lies clearly outside the pattern of the rest of the data set
An anomaly should be investigated and, if due to a measurement error, excluded before further analysis

nodes.label: Net decline as a ratio after multiple half-lives (HT)
nodes.objective: Calculate the net decline, expressed as a ratio, in radioactive emission after a given number of half-lives.
essentialPoints: Each half-life halves the remaining activity/number of nuclei
Net decline after n half-lives = (1/2)^n of original, expressed as a ratio

nodes.label: Evaluating uses of radiation for internal organ exploration
nodes.objective: Evaluate the choice and use of radiation sources for exploring internal organs, weighing benefits against risks.
essentialPoints: Benefit: enables diagnosis without invasive surgery
Risk: patient exposure to ionising radiation, choice of isotope (half-life, penetration, ionising power) matters

nodes.label: Evaluating uses of radiation for tissue control/destruction
nodes.objective: Evaluate the use of radiation for controlling or destroying unwanted tissue, weighing benefits against risks.
essentialPoints: Benefit: can target and destroy cancerous tissue
Risk: damage to surrounding healthy tissue, side effects of exposure

nodes.label: Importance of peer review for radiation research findings
nodes.objective: Explain why findings on the effects of radiation on humans must be published and peer reviewed.
essentialPoints: Findings must be published and shared with other scientists
Peer review allows checking of findings before wider acceptance

nodes.label: Controlled chain reaction (reactor) vs uncontrolled (weapon)
nodes.objective: Distinguish a controlled chain reaction in a nuclear reactor from the uncontrolled chain reaction in a nuclear weapon explosion.
essentialPoints: In a nuclear reactor, the chain reaction is controlled to regulate energy release
In a nuclear weapon, an uncontrolled chain reaction causes an explosion

nodes.label: Magnification equation
nodes.objective: Recall and apply magnification = image height / object height.
essentialPoints: magnification = image height ÷ object height
Magnification has no units (it is a ratio); heights measured in same units

nodes.label: Procedure: investigating magnification produced by convex lenses
nodes.objective: Carry out an investigation into the magnification produced by a range of convex lenses.
essentialPoints: Set up an illuminated object, convex lens and screen on an optical bench
Measure object height, image height, and object/image distances for different lenses or distances
Repeat for a range of lenses/distances to compare magnification

nodes.label: Application: calculating current drawn for a given power output
nodes.objective: Calculate the current drawn from the input supply to provide a particular power output.
essentialPoints: Rearrange Vp×Ip = Vs×Is to find Ip given the required output power and Vp
Use given values of voltages/turns ratio together with the power equation

nodes.label: Advantage: high-voltage power transmission reduces transmission losses
nodes.objective: Relate the transformer equations to the advantages of transmitting power at high potential difference.
essentialPoints: For a fixed power, higher transmission voltage means lower current is needed
Lower current reduces energy losses (heating) in transmission cables, since transformers can step voltage up for transmission and down for use

nodes.label: Evaluating methods and suggesting improvements
nodes.objective: Evaluate an experimental method for validity and sufficiency of data, suggesting improvements and further investigations.
essentialPoints: Assess whether enough precise measurements were taken to support a conclusion
A valid method tests only the intended variable and controls others properly

nodes.label: Evaluating perceived risks of nuclear radiation use
nodes.objective: Evaluate perceived risks of using nuclear radiation in relation to given data and consequences.
essentialPoints: Perceived risk may differ from actual/statistical risk based on data
Evaluation must weigh consequences (benefits vs harms) using provided data, not just public perception

nodes.label: Drawing/interpreting fission and chain reaction diagrams
nodes.objective: Draw or interpret diagrams representing nuclear fission and how a chain reaction may occur.
essentialPoints: Diagram shows neutron absorbed by nucleus, splitting into two nuclei plus neutrons and gamma rays
Diagram shows released neutrons triggering further fission events in a branching pattern

nodes.label: Application: calculating magnification from lens investigation data
nodes.objective: Calculate magnification from measured image and object heights obtained from the lens investigation.
essentialPoints: Substitute measured image height and object height into the magnification equation
Interpret resulting magnification value (greater than 1 = enlarged, less than 1 = diminished)

nodes.label: Communicating scientific rationale, methods and conclusions
nodes.objective: Present coherent, logically structured reports of investigations including rationale, method, findings and conclusions.
essentialPoints: A scientific report should logically link rationale, method, results and conclusion
Presentation may use verbal, diagrammatic, graphical, numerical or symbolic forms as appropriate
